author: Radde, 1863
habitat: 강 하구, 농경지, 해안가 개활지의 초지
summary: 아주 드물게 지나가는 나그네새로, 중부 이북 지역을 통과하는 모습이 관찰된다. 강 하구, 농경지, 해안가 트인 땅의 풀밭에 머물며 곤충, 작은 포유류, 새, 개구리, 도마뱀 등을 잡아먹는다. 국외에서는 중국 동북부, 아무르, 우수리, 몽골, 시베리아 북부에 분포한다.

points.en: red lower belly and undertail coverts (male)
black flight feathers and tail tip

sexes.male: 온몸이 어두운 회색이고 아랫배와 아래꼬리덮깃이 붉다. 날 때 흰 아래날개덮깃이 뚜렷하게 드러난다.
sexes.female: 윗면이 회색이고 뺨이 희며, 흰 아랫면에 검은 무늬가 빽빽하다. 아랫배의 적갈색은 더 흐리다.

art.subject: Amur Falcon (Falco amurensis), adult male, as seen in Korea on passage in May and from September to October: entire plumage dark slate-grey, slightly paler on the breast and belly; thighs, lower belly and undertail coverts rufous-red; underwing coverts pure white, contrasting with blackish-grey flight feathers; tail dark grey, darkest towards the tip. Bill short and hooked, dark grey with a paler base; bare cere and eye-ring orange-red; iris dark brown; legs and feet orange-red.
art.pose: perched on a low post, scanning the grass for prey
art.scene: Korean migration-season grassland on open coastal farmland near a river mouth; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched: dark slate-grey body, rufous-red thighs, lower belly and undertail coverts, orange-red cere, eye-ring and legs, wingtips reaching the tail tip
adult male, flight from below: pure white underwing coverts contrasting with blackish flight feathers, rufous-red vent, dark grey tail darker at the tip

adult female, side view perched: grey upperparts barred darker, dark grey crown, short dark moustachial stripe, white cheeks and throat, whitish underparts densely spotted and barred black, pale orange-buff thighs and vent, orange cere and legs
art.build: Small, slender falcon, 29–33cm, about kestrel-sized, a little shorter than a pigeon in body but with much longer wings. Rounded head, short neck, short hooked bill. Legs short, orange-red. At rest the long pointed wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail medium length, rounded-square at the tip. Agile flight on long pointed wings; often hovers and hawks insects over grassland, and perches on wires, posts and bare trees.
avoid: Do not paint a rufous back or spotted brown upperparts; that is Common Kestrel.
Do not paint grey or dark underwing coverts on the male; they are pure white.
Do not paint yellow cere or legs; they are orange-red.
Do not give the male a moustachial stripe or streaked underparts.
